label: STRICT_PAST_ACCESSIBILITY_1: For a supplied Preorder T and designated now, the frame carrier is the…
definition: For a supplied Preorder T and designated now, the frame carrier is the subtype of times t with t=now or t<now. Accessibility from t to s means s<t. Transitivity ensures each earlier witness remains inside this past-through-now carrier. It is a concrete construction of the existing Frame, not a new temporal syntax or causal relation.
note: Owner-approved bounded temporal interpretation of the existing Frame/order vocabulary; no new Lean semantic primitive. See StrictPastFrame and the unchanged inline frames in Modal.PastSerialityCertificate. Time points are not identified with modal alternative complete histories or causal graph vertices. No physical-past, duration or event-count claim. Declaration completion names the concrete existing Frame construction, with its original carrier and orientation; it does not wrap an unconstrained relation. The inclusive carrier remains all T, as in the frozen certificate. Nat controls are examples only, not restrictions on the universally quantified Preorder.
